overview: Based on the published agenda, the Kronenwetter Plan Commission was scheduled to meet on August 17, 2026, to address multiple zoning and development matters including a twin home ordinance, conditional use permit, site plan review, and septic tank regulations. The meeting was set to consider both old and new business items affecting residential and commercial development in the village.

agenda.item: Twin Home Zero Lot Line Ordinance
Land Use and Zoning Appeals Process
Future Review of Zoning and Subdivisions Codes

discussions.item: Twin Home Zero Lot Line Ordinance
discussions.body: The Plan Commission was scheduled to discuss and take possible action on a Twin Home Zero Lot Line Ordinance. This item was listed under old business, indicating it was set for continued consideration from a previous meeting.

The Commission was set to review and consider possible action on a Conditional Use Permit related to Knetter Pond. This matter was expected to involve discussion of how the property could be developed or used under conditional approval.

The Plan Commission was scheduled to examine a site plan for a Marathon County Garage facility. The Commission was expected to consider design, layout, and compliance with village zoning and development standards.

The Commission was set to discuss and potentially act on a new or revised Septic Tank Ordinance. This regulatory item was expected to address standards and requirements for septic systems within the village.

discussions.item: Land Use and Zoning Appeals Process
discussions.body: The Plan Commission was scheduled to discuss the Land Use and Zoning Appeals Process. This item was set for review of procedures related to how appeals of zoning decisions are handled in the village.

discussions.item: Future Review of Zoning and Subdivisions Codes
discussions.body: The Commission was set to discuss and consider a future comprehensive review of the village's Zoning and Subdivisions Codes. This item was expected to establish parameters for an upcoming comprehensive code assessment.

publicComment: Public comment was on the agenda, limited to 15 minutes total with three minutes per person.
